author: Athul Prem
question: Which rigid-template contents and remainders associate with the dominant 1 GHz reflected conversion pair, and how do they change between the saved z4/z6 sections?

physical_inputs.coordinate_convention: x propagation, y in-plane width, z thickness; saved lab-aligned crystal tensor unchanged
physical_inputs.material_policy: Nominal fixed-property Ge, not measured mK/4 K sample data

definitions.template_score: abs(q^H M u)^2 / ((q^H M q)*(u^H M u)); mass-weighted shape overlap, not power
definitions.template_remainder_fraction: Content outside all four tested rigid templates; retain mixed or higher section shapes
definitions.converted_R: Sum of reflected power except the unique negative-wavenumber partner of the incident root
definitions.converted_T: Sum of transmitted power except the incident positive-wavenumber root
definitions.complex_alignment: S_z6_aligned[out,in] = exp(i*phase_out) * S_z6_raw[out,in] / exp(i*phase_in), using accepted signed section overlaps
definitions.signed_delta: z6 minus z4, at the original physical end planes

interpretation: The dominant converted pair includes z6 root 1837 with Tz score 0.934194230954 and root 1877 with Tz score 0.000274824472 and four-template remainder 0.999725175527. Both have large z kinetic content, but the latter is not represented by these rigid templates. Do not label both as simple z-flexural branches. Directed pair powers decrease about 3.86148% in this finite z4/z6 increment, without a mechanism or uncertainty claim.
